query_ground_truth.workflow_task: Create customized application emails with resume and cover letter PDFs, stage them as Outlook drafts, update attachments and body text, then send the finalized drafts after confirmation.
query_ground_truth.query: send finalized outlook email drafts after user confirmation
query_ground_truth.intent: Send out the staged email drafts once confirmation is received.

request.query: send finalized outlook email drafts after user confirmation

results.use_case: send finalized outlook email drafts after user confirmation
results.execution_guidance: IMPORTANT: Follow the recommended plan below. Extract steps before execution, adapt to your current context, execute sequentially with current_step parameter, and check known pitfalls to avoid errors.
recommended_plan_steps: [Optional (if you don’t need a draft/review)] [Step]: Send the email directly using OUTLOOK_SEND_EMAIL (confirm final to/cc, subject, body, and whether content is HTML).
[Optional (if you want deliverability/recipient warnings before sending)] [Prerequisite]: Check recipient guidance using OUTLOOK_GET_MAIL_TIPS (review tips and adjust recipients if needed).

[Required (if message_id is unknown and you need an existing draft)] [Prerequisite]: Locate Drafts using OUTLOOK_GET_DRAFTS_MAIL_FOLDER then use OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDER_MESSAGES (follow @odata.nextLink pagination) to find the right draft and capture message_id.
[Fallback (if draft lookup fails or no suitable draft exists)] [Fallback]: Create a new draft using OUTLOOK_CREATE_DRAFT (capture returned message_id).

[Optional (if recipients/subject/body need changes or attachments must be added)] [Next Step]: Update the draft using OUTLOOK_UPDATE_EMAIL and/or add files using OUTLOOK_ADD_MAIL_ATTACHMENT (apply to the message_id you will send).

[Required (only after explicit user confirmation)] [Step]: Send the chosen draft using OUTLOOK_SEND_DRAFT (use final message_id; if a 404 occurs, re-locate the draft via OUTLOOK_GET_DRAFTS_MAIL_FOLDER + OUTLOOK_LIST_MAIL_FOLDER_MESSAGES and re-confirm before retrying).
known_pitfalls: [OUTLOOK_SEND_EMAIL] Success may be HTTP 202 with null/minimal body; treat as success and don’t retry (duplicate-send risk).
[OUTLOOK_SEND_DRAFT] Success may return {} or minimal content; rely on HTTP success and avoid blind retries; invalid/expired message_id may surface as 404.
[OUTLOOK_SEND_EMAIL] Validation errors if required recipient field isn’t `to`; `to` should be a string (not a list) to avoid “Input should be a valid string”.
[OUTLOOK_SEND_EMAIL] If sending HTML, set the HTML flag correctly or recipients may see raw markup.
[OUTLOOK_CREATE_DRAFT] Drafts may be created without recipients; ensure recipients exist before attempting delivery (update draft or use OUTLOOK_SEND_EMAIL).

OUTLOOK_SEND_DRAFT.description: Tool to send an existing draft message. Use after creating a draft when you want to deliver it to recipients immediately. Example: Send a draft message with ID 'AAMkAG…'.

user_id.description: The user's email address or 'me' to represent the authenticated user.

message_id.description: The unique identifier of the draft message to send.

OUTLOOK_SEND_EMAIL.description: Sends an email with subject, body, recipients, and optional attachments via Microsoft Graph API. Supports comma-separated email addresses in the to_email field for multiple recipients. Accepts either a single file or a list of files as attachments. Attachments require a non-empty file with valid name and mimetype.

to.description: The primary recipient's email address(es). You can provide a single email or multiple emails separated by commas. Valid email addresses will be extracted from strings containing extra text. Format: name@domain.com

examples: Hello team, please find the attached report.
body.description: The content of the email body as a plain string (plain text or HTML based on `is_html`). Do not pass structured objects; provide only the raw text/HTML content.

is_html.description: Specifies if the email body is HTML; `True` for HTML, `False` for plain text.

subject.description: The subject line of the email.

to_name.description: The display name of the primary recipient.

user_id.description: The user's email address or the alias 'me' to represent the authenticated user.

cc_emails.description: List of email addresses for CC recipients. Each email should be a separate string in the array. Do NOT pass comma-separated values as a single string.
